pl-l3d12c1-d1e117.summary: Asks whether God could have assumed another man, or a man from elsewhere than the race of Adam.

pl-l3d12c1-d1e120.summary: Answers that the Word could have assumed another soul and other flesh, since that soul and flesh were assumed by grace alone; Augustine says the highest grace among temporal things is that man was joined to God in unity of person. So God could have taken another soul and flesh, and flesh from outside Adam's race.
claims: The soul and flesh of Christ were assumed by grace alone.
God could have assumed other soul and flesh, even from outside Adam's race.

pl-l3d12c1-d1e126.summary: Cites Augustine, De Trinitate XIII: God could have taken a man from elsewhere to be mediator, not from Adam, who bound the race by his sin, just as he created the first man from no race; he could have created another by whom the victor of the first would be conquered. But he judged it better to take a man from the conquered race to defeat man's enemy, and yet from a Virgin whose conception was preceded by the Spirit, not flesh, by faith, not lust, without the concupiscence through which others contract original sin; her virginity was made fruitful by believing, not by intercourse.
claims: God could have created a new man as mediator.
It was better to take a man from the conquered race.

pl-l3d12c1-d1e136.summary: Concludes that these texts show God could have assumed another man and a man from elsewhere.
claims: God could have assumed another man, from elsewhere.

pl-l3d12c1.summary: Asks whether God could have assumed another man, or a man from elsewhere than Adam's race. He could have assumed another soul and other flesh, since that soul and flesh were assumed by grace alone, and could have taken flesh from outside Adam's stock, as Augustine says in De Trinitate XIII; but he judged it better to take a man from the conquered race to conquer the enemy, yet from a Virgin whose conception was preceded by faith, not lust, without concupiscence.
claims: God could have assumed another soul and other flesh.
God could have taken flesh from outside Adam's race.
It was more fitting to take a man from the conquered race.
